scene.metaphor: A browser-sized archive cabinet where a hidden query mechanism snaps the correct document forward from a dense local stack, like a miniature indexed library that answers instantly without any server behind it.
scene.setting: Polished studio tabletop set in a cool-gray workspace, with a tiny handmade cabinet built from matte gray card, milled wood, and translucent acrylic, staged against a soft gradient backdrop with generous negative space.
scene.frozen_incident: Tal has just slid a mint-colored query lever; one narrow drawer in a row of identical drawers has popped open and a single document folder is springing forward while the others remain neatly shut, implying instant matching and no wasted motion.
physical_materials: one restrained warm accent on a folder edge
scene.image_instruction: Create a polished studio tabletop photograph of Tal Perry as a recognizable operator: curly dark hair, salt-and-pepper beard, warm direct smile, seen from the waist up leaning into a miniature cabinet. He wears a modern sleeveless top in muted coral only as the single warm accent; everything else stays cool gray, cobalt, and mint. The set is a handmade browser-sized archive: a low horizontal row of many tiny identical drawers made from matte gray chipboard and brushed metal, with translucent acrylic fronts and cobalt paper tabs, sitting on a felt base. Tal’s hand has just pulled a mint lever, and in the frozen instant one drawer has snapped open and a single folder/document is sliding forward while the surrounding drawers remain closed, making the “instant match from a dense local archive” idea literal. Light it like serious editorial product photography with crisp tonal separation, soft shadow falloff, and generous negative space. Keep the composition lateral and banner-friendly, with one dominant cabinet silhouette that reads clearly at thumbnail size.
